title: "Uninstall or Manage Add-Ons…" is shown for apps without AppStream metadata and silently does nothing when clicked
line: Kickoff no longer offers "Uninstall or Manage Add-Ons…" for apps that have no AppStream entry, where it did nothing; Tobias's open MR !7390 does this and works.
explanation: Kicker's app menus added "Uninstall or Manage Add-Ons…" for every app as long as an appstream:// handler (Discover) is installed. Only on click did it look up the app's AppStream component, and when there was none (e.g. LibreOffice's start center) it returned without doing anything. Tobias Fella's open MR !7390 loads the AppStream pool once in a background thread at startup, maps each desktop id to its component id, and adds the action only for apps that have one; the click handler uses the same map, so the menu no longer blocks on loading the pool either.

commits.message:
kicker: hide "uninstall" action for apps without appstream metadata

The action was offered for every app, but clicking it did nothing when
AppStream has no component for the app. Look up the component ids in the
background at startup and only show the action when one exists.

BUG: 528629

media.caption: Pure master: right-click "LibreOffice" (start center, no AppStream component) offers Uninstall or Manage Add-Ons…
Pure master: after clicking it, the menu closes and nothing opens (checked for 10 s)
With the fix: the same menu has no Uninstall or Manage Add-Ons… entry

review.text: Tobias's MR !7390 fixes the cause: the action was added without checking for an AppStream component. Loading the pool once off the main thread and using a desktop-id to component-id map for both the check and the click is clean and also stops the click from blocking. The screenshots show the action gone for the start center and kept for Math. The only trade-off, apps installed after startup getting no action until restart, was already there before.
